title: Decode: MegaMoE NVFP4 EP32 + shared-expert overlap
shape: D3-32 r24 1-node slice (EP4 emulating EP32: 28 active experts/rank split 14+14 over the die halves, EP32 MegaMoE records via knob_world_size; SP shard 96 MoE tokens/GPU, top-16, L~135K, k=3); ms = 23-layer slice x4 (92 MoE layers)
basis: MEASURED in-step, NVFP4 checkpoint, same harness (runs/D-MOE/sb = stepbench + die-split active set): baseline = int b31121cf56 + D-MOE 01ace2323a with the slice picking the EP4 prefill records (runs/D-MOE/step_d/base-die2-nv-r8r16r24-prof: MegaMoE exposed 1824/1846/1786 us per 23 layers at r8/r16/r24); current = 4b58015c31 with the slice on the EP32 records (step_d/hook-die2-nv-r8r16r24-prof: 1504/1461/1603; step 6460/8634/10647 us); achievable nvfp4_modelopt 1086/1201/1316. NOTE: the gain is the slice now measuring the configuration production EP32 already runs (128-token N128 bucket, phase_interleave, die-local, full grid); it is a measurement fix, not new kernel speed. INFRA trial-9ccf8ab (old emulation, all active experts on die 0) read 1763 at r24.
gap_analysis: r24 remaining gap 1603 -> 1316 (target 1448): ~12.5 us/layer exposed above achievable. Per layer in-step (EP4-emulated EP32 config): router kernel ~7 us + stage ~3 us + main persistent kernel + separate top-k reduce ~3.6 us; the main kernel shares SMs/HBM with the side-stream shared expert (serializing it or running it beside the MoE front only were both measured worse). Stamps (EP4 graph replay, T96): after all sizes are visible the main kernel needs ~55 us (1 GPU ~40): token pull up to 11.6 us, CTA end spread ~9 us, tail NVLink barrier ~1-3 us; router publish_sizes 3.4 us. E1 (entry L2 prefetch of the FC1 stream head) measured neutral/negative: the front is not where the time goes. SOL path: E2 fold the top-k reduce into the kernel tail (removes a kernel boundary ~3 us/layer), E3 finer/LPT last FC2 wave (CTA end spread 9 -> ~2 us), E4 router size publication as one multicast release (EP32: 31 peers), E5 run the shared expert as extra work items of the persistent grid instead of a concurrent cuBLAS kernel. EP32 dispatch/combine (+~17 us/layer on Hecate) needs the 8-node hold.
inefficiencies: FIXED on the branch: D3-32 decode used DeepGEMM fp8_fp4 MegaMoE (149 us/layer exposed at r24 in the slice); kimi_k3_mega_moe on the re-vendored kernel: 68 us/layer exposed
MEASURED (stamps, 1 GPU T96): weights stream only after the router publishes sizes (~3 us after the call starts); at T>=4 every local expert is active so the weight stream does not depend on routing
MEASURED: CTA finish imbalance ~4 us at the end of the stream (median vs max last-MMA end), then a ~1.2 us tail barrier
MEASURED: separate BF16 top-k reduce kernel ~2.7 us and NVFP4 quant/stage kernel ~1.9 us per call around the persistent kernel
MEASURED (Hecate EP32 vs 1 GPU): ~17 us/call of dispatch/combine latency not hidden behind the weight stream at EP32
MEASURED: stream phase itself ~85-90% of the die-local HBM rate (weights die-localized + die_split active)
In-tree D3-32 runs vendored DeepGEMM fp8_fp4 (no NVFP4 EP32 backend); shared experts serial on that path (fix: megamoe_rubin re-vendor, landed on the branch)
